summary: Furail Brewing Co., LLC (client, buyer) acquired substantially all brewing assets of Dromuv Craft Ales, Inc., a Hudson Valley craft brewery, under an Asset Purchase Agreement signed September 8, 2026 and closed September 30, 2026. The assets include a 30-barrel brewhouse, finished beer and keg inventory, core recipes and trademarks, distributor agreements, and the head brewer's employment agreement. The $8,400,000 purchase price was paid partly through a $2,100,000 Seller Note. A closing-date Side Letter, an IP Assignment with a recipe license-back, a Bill of Sale, the head brewer agreement, and a November 9, 2026 Furail board consent complete the operative set. Six issues are planted: an uncapped buyer indemnity created by the Side Letter, an effective survival period cut to 90 days through the Seller Note, a missing assignment consent from the head brewer, a freely assignable recipe license, a lapsed inventory rejection window, and split governing law and forum for setoff disputes.

issues.label: uncapped indemnity
issues.description: APA Section 9.3(c) makes Buyer indemnify Seller for Assumed Liabilities. APA Section 9.5 caps Buyer's indemnity at 10% of the Purchase Price only for claims under Sections 9.3(a) and (b), and says claims under Section 9.3(c) are not subject to any cap. Read alone, that is ordinary, because Assumed Liabilities are normally post-closing obligations Buyer bears anyway. Side Letter Section 2 amends the definition of Assumed Liabilities to cover all liabilities under the Distributor Agreements, whether arising before, on or after the Closing Date, including termination or compensation payments under beer franchise laws. Under APA Section 11.12 the Side Letter prevails over the APA. Read together, these provisions move Dromuv's pre-closing distributor liabilities, such as franchise-law termination payments, onto Furail through an indemnity that has no cap. They also shrink Seller's indemnity for Excluded Liabilities.
detect_terms: whether arising before, on or after the Closing Date
issues.expected_finding: Because the Side Letter, which prevails under APA Section 11.12, extends Assumed Liabilities to pre-closing distributor and franchise-law liabilities, and APA Section 9.5 excludes Section 9.3(c) claims from any cap, Furail faces uncapped indemnity exposure for Dromuv's pre-closing distributor liabilities; the Side Letter definition should be limited to post-closing liabilities or those claims brought under the cap.
detect_terms2: shall not be subject to any cap

issues.label: indemnity survival gap
issues.description: APA Section 9.1 says Seller's representations survive until the earlier of (a) 12 months after the Closing and (b) the date on which the Seller Note is paid in full, and Section 9.4 requires claims to be noticed before survival expires. Seller Note Section 2 makes the full principal due ninety (90) days after the Closing Date. The Closing Date is September 30, 2026 (Bill of Sale Section 1). Read together, the representations, including the inventory, recipe ownership and environmental/wastewater representations, expire no later than December 29, 2026, or earlier if the Note is prepaid. That is far too short to find most breaches, and Furail's setoff leverage against the Note ends at the same moment.
detect_terms: the date on which the Seller Note is paid in full
issues.expected_finding: Read with the Seller Note's 90-day maturity, APA Section 9.1 cuts Seller's representation survival to no later than December 29, 2026 (90 days after the September 30, 2026 Closing), leaving Furail almost no time to bring indemnity claims; the survival trigger should be decoupled from Note payment and set at a fixed period of at least 12 months.
detect_terms2: ninety (90) days after the Closing Date

issues.label: change of control consent
issues.description: APA Section 2.1(c) lists Tomasz Kerrevan's head brewer employment agreement among the Assigned Contracts. APA Section 4.4 represents that no consent, approval or notice of any third party is required to assign the Assigned Contracts other than the distributor consents. Section 8.2 of the employment agreement (D2) says Employer may not assign it, whether by change of control of Employer or sale of all or substantially all of Employer's assets, without Employee's prior written consent. It also says the non-compete and recipe confidentiality covenants shall not inure to the benefit of any successor absent that consent. Nothing in the folder shows Kerrevan's consent, and the Closing occurred on September 30, 2026. Read together, Furail may be unable to enforce the head brewer's non-compete and recipe confidentiality, which protect the core value of the acquired recipes. Its only fallback is an indemnity claim for breach of Section 4.4, and that claim is itself limited by the short survival period.
detect_terms: sale of all or substantially all of Employer's assets
shall not inure to the benefit of any successor
issues.expected_finding: The head brewer agreement requires Kerrevan's written consent to an assignment on a sale of substantially all of Dromuv's assets, the APA treated it as an Assigned Contract without any listed consent, and no consent was obtained, so Furail may be unable to enforce his non-compete and recipe confidentiality covenants; Furail should obtain his written consent or a new agreement promptly and preserve an indemnity claim for breach of APA Section 4.4.
detect_terms2: no consent, approval or notice of any third party

issues.label: unrestricted assignment
issues.description: IP Assignment Agreement Section 5 grants Dromuv a license-back of the acquired Legacy Recipes for its retained Kingston taproom. Section 5.3 lets Licensee assign the license, in whole or in part, to any Person without Licensor's consent. Dromuv could therefore transfer rights to Furail's core recipes to a competing brewery, which undermines the exclusivity Furail paid for.
detect_terms: to any Person without the consent of Licensor
issues.expected_finding: The recipe license-back in IP Assignment Agreement Section 5.3 is freely assignable by Dromuv, including to a competitor, so it should be made non-assignable without Furail's consent (except to a successor to the taproom) and limited to on-premises use at the retained taproom.

issues.label: expired notice window
issues.description: Side Letter Section 3 gives Furail the right to reject Nonconforming Inventory (off-spec finished beer) by delivering a rejection notice within thirty (30) days after the Closing Date, and makes that right Buyer's sole and exclusive remedy for nonconforming finished beer inventory. Under APA Section 11.12 the Side Letter controls. The Closing Date is September 30, 2026 (Bill of Sale), so the window closed on October 30, 2026. The Furail Board Consent (D6) is dated November 9, 2026. It is the first document authorizing officers to deliver a rejection notice for 1,140 barrels of off-spec IPA. It also records that Seller has asserted Furail's rights have lapsed, and that the Company does not accept that position and reserves its rights. The rejection right appears to have expired. Because the Side Letter makes it the exclusive remedy, Furail may have lost any recovery for the off-spec inventory unless it obtains a waiver or extension or attacks the exclusivity.
detect_terms: within thirty (30) days after the Closing Date
issues.expected_finding: The 30-day Inventory Rejection Notice window ran from the September 30, 2026 Closing and expired on October 30, 2026, before the November 9, 2026 board consent authorized the notice for 1,140 barrels. Because the Side Letter makes that right the exclusive remedy, Furail risks losing any recovery. Consistent with the board's recorded objection, Furail should deliver the notice immediately, seek Dromuv's written waiver or an extension, and assess arguments against the exclusivity.

issues.label: governing law mismatch
issues.description: APA Section 11.9 chooses New York law and exclusive New York County courts for all disputes, including indemnity claims. Seller Note Section 10 chooses Delaware law and the exclusive jurisdiction of the Court of Chancery for any claim relating to the Note, including any right of setoff asserted against it. APA Section 11.12 provides that the Seller Note controls on matters relating to the Note, so the APA's precedence clause does not cure the conflict. Read together, Furail's main indemnity remedy, setting off claims against Note payments, would be litigated in Delaware under Delaware law, while the underlying indemnity claim must be brought in New York. That creates parallel proceedings and a risk of inconsistent outcomes, and lets Dromuv pursue payment in Delaware while Furail's claims proceed in New York.
detect_terms: laws of the State of Delaware
any right of setoff asserted against this Note
issues.expected_finding: The Seller Note's Delaware law and exclusive Chancery forum, which control Note matters under APA Section 11.12, split Furail's setoff rights from its New York-governed indemnity claims under APA Section 11.9, so the Note should be conformed to New York law and the APA forum.
